items.title: 17 opportunities auto-abandoned in one batch sweep (~$87K, mostly warm)
items.summary: A single automated sweep at 12:06 UTC today abandoned 17 open opportunities at once; 15 were tagged lead: warm with a mobile quote already sent, worth roughly $87,296 combined. The ages at abandonment (~66 days for the largest cohort) don't line up with the documented 80-day Later-Date-Warm threshold - looks like a periodic bulk cleanup rather than the continuous per-day rule, and several of these read as still-viable warm quotes, not dead leads.

items.title: Abandon-threshold mismatch: batch fired at ~66 days vs documented 80
items.summary: The 15 warm/mobile-quote opportunities auto-abandoned today entered Later Date (Warm) between 2026-05-27 and 2026-06-08 (11-day spread) but were all closed in one pass today - roughly 66 days for the newest of the cohort, well short of the documented 2x/80-day rule. Either ghl-workflow.json's threshold is stale or abandonment runs as a periodic sweep, not continuously; worth confirming against the live GHL automation.

leads_by_source._note: Open opportunities only, source field as GHL stores it verbatim. Casing/concatenation quirks (Store vs store, onlineMeta Ad) are GHL data as-is, not normalized.

leads_by_tag._note: All 1,802 distinct contacts across every opportunity status (open/won/lost/abandoned), not mutually exclusive - a contact can carry more than one lead:* tag at once (e.g. a re-categorized lead keeping its old tag).

avg_days_in_stage._note: Open-status opportunities only, days since lastStageChangeAt (falls back to createdAt). Far Out (Cold) and Postponed averages are inflated by a large backlog of very old, apparently never-swept records (see stragglers).

meeting_window_summary._note: 59% of the 49 open Meeting-Scheduled opportunities are already stale_lead-tagged, underscoring why Albert is designing a follow-up sequence for this stage.
